sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:29

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:29:1
items.html: Atik and Arich, who are called the Keter of Atzilut, take between the two of them the two phases: This is because the whole essence of the MA is in order to correct the BON, and hence we call the names of the Partzufim according to the relation that is in them from the side of the BON. However, the states of the Partzufim are according to the relation of the MA, since it is the male in them. That is to say, all the light that is bestowed in the Partzufim is MA, as above, and hence it is certainly what governs the arrangement in them. Therefore, since Atik and Arich are both the Keter of Nekudim, they are accordingly reckoned as the Keter of Atzilut as well. Yet their state is necessarily according to the relation of the MA in them, in which the Keter of MA is the male of Atik, and the Hochma of MA is the male of AA. And it has already been explained that because of the ascent of the bottom Hey to Keter, Hochma too went out from the Rosh [head] of Keter. Hence the Partzuf AA is regarded as having the relation of a Guf [body] toward the Partzuf Atik, since it is the Hochma of MA, and it clothes the Guf of Atik — even though according to the BON they are both Keter. And this is for the reason mentioned above, that the states are under the governance of the MA, since it is the owner of the light in the Partzufim.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:29:2
items.html:
The Keter and the Hochma of MA for their male side, etc.: We must thoroughly understand this great change that is made here, that the male and the female of a single Partzuf, who necessarily must be in one degree, should be from two Sefirot — and moreover, that the male should be from the Sefira of Hochma and the female from the Sefira of Keter. Also the matter of the division of the Sefira of Keter between two Partzufim, and why Atik did not take the lower half of the Sefira of Keter of BON as well.
And first we shall explain why, in AVI of Nekudim, in the coupling of Gadlut, all three Roshim of Nekudim joined to AVI as ten Sefirot of Rosh at the level of Keter, whereas here, in the new MA, it was not so. Rather, even in its own coupling of Gadlut, in which through the illumination of AB the bottom Hey went out from the forehead and returned to its place in the Peh [mouth], and the ten Sefirot emerged at the level of Keter — even so, this availed only the Sefira of Keter alone, and all the remaining nine lower Sefirot did not return to Rosh. And moreover, they received nothing at all from this coupling, as the ARI writes: when Atik was corrected, nothing at all below Atik was corrected; and likewise, when AA was corrected, nothing at all below him was corrected; and so too AVI, and so too ZON, as above.
And you already know the root of the new MA, which is the screen of the Guf of Nekudim, which raised the records of the seven kings, and the four posteriors of AVI and YESHSUT, and the posterior of NHY of Keter, and brought them to the Rosh of SAG, to the forehead, which is the Bina of Galgalta of SAG. And upon it emerged a level of ZA of clothing and a level of Malchut of coarseness, from Bina of Keter upward, as above (page 613, the passage beginning “And you already”). And since the place of the coupling is Bina of Keter, they therefore received there the posterior of Bina, and they were corrected back to back, in the secret of the correction of the lines, which are called “three within three.” For since there is here only the level of Malchut of coarseness, there is therefore only a level of NHY, since the level of HGT is only clothing, which has no vessels. Hence HGT were compelled to clothe inside NHY, and this is called “three within three,” or Ibur [impregnation].
Now, from this level of Ibur only the Ketarim in all the records that ascended there as MAN [Mayin Nukvin] were corrected — and not all the ten Sefirot that are in Keter, but only from Bina upward alone. The reason is that the illumination of the posterior of Bina that is in them did not let them expand to ZON, since the power of the posterior of Bina exists only before she expands to the illumination of ZON; but when she expands to the illumination of ZON, she is already compelled to cease her posterior and to couple with Hochma, to receive from him the illumination of Hochma for the ZON, as above (page 502, the passage beginning “And you should know”). Therefore ZON are found here in that same state of the ZAT of Nekudim, in which the illumination of the Rosh did not reach them because of the illumination of the posterior of AVI. And you find that not only did Hochma go out from Rosh to Guf, but the ZON of Keter itself also went out from Rosh to Guf, because the bottom Hey stands in Bina of Keter, as explained. And even the illumination of “three within three” did not reach them.
And there is one further matter here in the new MA: since the bottom Hey ascended to Keter, the Parsa received a great strengthening. For as long as the Parsa was from the bottom Hey in the Einayim, it had no power to endure even at the time of the coupling of Gadlut of AB-SAG. For when the new light of the coupling of AB-SAG descended and brought the bottom Hey down from the Einayim to the Peh, and breached the Parsa, and illuminated in Nekudim, as above in part 7 — then the Parsa had no power to detain the light from expanding into BYA, and this is why the breaking occurred, as is known. But now that the power of the Parsa has been doubled because of the bottom Hey that ascended to Keter, it has grown far stronger, so that even the coupling of Gadlut, which brings the bottom Hey down from the forehead to the Peh, does not annul the boundary of Katnut of the Parsa in the least; rather, only the vessels grow.
Therefore, even with the new light that descended from the coupling of AB-SAG, which brought the bottom Hey down from the forehead to the Peh, and the ten Sefirot of the Rosh of Atik emerged at the level of Keter, this primordial boundary of Katnut was not annulled on account of it, and the ZON of Keter did not return to Rosh. Rather, through their reception of the level of the Rosh from above downward, the vessels grew, so that the HGT of the Guf became KHB, and the NHY became HGT, and new NHY emerged for them. However, they remained in Guf, and the status of Rosh did not return upon them as it was in AVI of Nekudim. Therefore, although Atik was corrected in a complete level of ten Sefirot up to Keter, still nothing of this reached the Partzuf AA, since even his own Guf did not return to Rosh, and all the more so the remaining nine lower Sefirot. Hence this whole level of Keter emerged and expanded in the one Sefira of Keter alone, and the remaining Sefirot received nothing from it. And in the same way it was with the Sefira of Hochma, which expanded of itself, through the two couplings, Katnut and Gadlut, into RTS [Rosh-Toch-Sof], and nothing of it reached Bina at all, and so on in the same manner.
And with this you will understand that those ten Sefirot at the level of Keter, which emerged in the level of the looking of the Einayim of AVI, and which include within them all the other levels that emerged in Nekudim, come here in the new MA one after the other, in five separate couplings — that is, a separate level in each Sefira, in the manner explained above. Nor, moreover, in an equal level, as it was in the looking of the Einayim of AVI, but rather each one below the other: in Atik alone the level of Keter emerged, in AA the level of Hochma emerged, in AVI the level of Bina, and in ZON the level of ZA. And the reason is that every lower one emerges from the Guf of the upper one, since the bottom Hey is above it, as above. Thus the level of AA, which in relation to Keter is regarded as a Guf, is not reckoned as a Rosh except with respect to the Sefira of Hochma; and thus AA lacks the GAR [first three] of Yechida, since with respect to the light of Yechida it is reckoned as a Guf, as explained. So too AVI are reckoned as a Guf toward AA, who is Hochma, and they are reckoned as a Rosh only with respect to the new coupling that was made upon the screen of phase two, which is Bina. Yet all three Partzufim — Atik, AA and AVI — are reckoned as complete Partzufim of Rosh and Guf, for AA has a Rosh and GAR at least from the new coupling of phase three, and AVI have a Rosh and GAR from the new coupling of phase two — similar to the Partzufim Galgalta, AB, SAG, MA and BON of AK, where every lower one is a Guf to the upper one, yet with respect to itself it has a complete Rosh, as is known.
This is not so with ZON: since they emerged only at the level of ZA, which is Nefesh-Ruach, they therefore lack GAR entirely, and they emerged as a Guf without a Rosh. And you see the great diminution that came about because of the ascent of the bottom Hey to the forehead. For besides the Sefirot being divided, each and every Sefira emerging in a separate level of its own, they also emerged one below the other, until it caused ZA to emerge lacking a Rosh. But with the new light that descended from the coupling of AB-SAG in Nekudim, there emerged thereby in AVI ten Sefirot, KHB ZON, whose level was all equal, up to Keter, and even the Malchut among them.
In addition to the above, we must remember that there is a great difference between the vessels of GAR of Nekudim and the vessels of ZAT of Nekudim, for the vessels of GAR are from the first Hey and have nothing of the bottom Hey. And those vessels emerged through the illumination of NHY of AK by way of the Tabur, whereby the bottom Hey that was in the Einayim of Keter descended to the Peh of Nekudim, and AVI returned to Rosh. But since Ima desires Hassadim, she still does not turn her face to Aba to receive Hochma except by way of MAN. And these GAR are from the vessels of AVI, which have nothing of the bottom Hey, as above (Part 6, Inner Observation, item 9). The vessels of ZAT, however, emerged through the MAN of a Vav and a point from the Yesod of AK; and these MAN restored AVI to face to face, and they coupled upon the MAN and brought out a level of ten Sefirot from below upward at the level of Keter, which is called the looking of the Einayim of AVI, and from there downward they brought out the seven kings:
first the king of Daat, and after refinement to phase three they brought out the king of Hesed, and so forth, as is known. Hence only the level from below upward, which emerged through the MAN of the Yesod of AK, is what is reckoned as the Rosh of ZON — but not the levels that emerged before the MAN, from face to back, for these have no relation to ZON, since they have no part in the bottom Hey, as explained.
Thus it has been explained that in those ten Sefirot that emerged for AVI of Nekudim at the level of Keter, one must distinguish between the GAR in them, which have no connection with ZON, and the ZON in them, which are reckoned as the Rosh of the ZAT of Nekudim. And with this you will understand that those first three Partzufim — Atik, AA and AVI — that emerged in Nekudim have no further connection to the ZON of Atzilut, since they are from the GAR in the Roshim of AVI of Nekudim.
And with this you will understand that there are here three discernments in the ten Sefirot of Nekudim, and that there is a great difference between them in the manner of their correction. The first discernment is the Katnut that emerged in Nekudim through the ascent of the bottom Hey to the Einayim, that is, as much as emerged from the substance of their emanation, which is back to back alone. The second is the face to back that emerged in Nekudim through the illumination of the Tabur of AK, which brought the bottom Hey down from the Einayim of Keter of Nekudim to the Peh of Nekudim and restored AVI to Rosh — where Ima still remains in the posterior toward Aba, even though she became a complete Rosh, because she delights in Hesed. And the difference between the first discernment and the second is that in the first, when the bottom Hey was above AVI, AVI had only the level of ZON, as is known; but now they have the level of Keter, since the bottom Hey is in its place in the Peh. However, Ima, although she is able to receive the light of Hochma, still has an ingrained desire, by force of the nature of her emanation in direct light, whereby she craves only the light of Hassadim, as is known. And there is indeed a gain in this for the ZAT of Nekudim, for now they are able to receive the light of Hassadim from Ima in wholeness, these being the ten Sefirot at the level of ZA that expand to them from Ima, who has returned to Rosh. And remember this.
And the third discernment is the two Roshim that emerged in the GAR of Nekudim in face to face, that is, upon the MAN of a Vav and a point that they received from the Yesod of AK, along with their from-above-downward aspect, which is called the ZAT of Nekudim.
And the choicest of them is the first discernment, namely the back to back that remained in AVI of Nekudim, for they suffered nothing at all from the breaking, as above. And after them is the second discernment, namely the GAR of AVI that emerged in face to back, since they are clean of the bottom Hey, as above; and likewise the illumination of Ruach-Nefesh that expanded from them to ZA is of that same merit. Hence in the two discernments mentioned above there is a great distinction, for after they were corrected in Atzilut their correction remained permanently, and the flaw of the lower ones causes them no departure whatsoever. This is not so with the third discernment: since it comes through the MAN of the Yesod of AK, which is a Vav and a point — that is, the bottom Hey is present there — its correction is therefore not permanent. Rather, all the corrections that come in this discernment rise and fall according to the deeds of the lower ones. And remember all the above, for it is an introduction by which to understand the continuation of the words of the ARI that lie before us.
